title: The Relevance of “Set and Setting” for Medical Cannabis Patients in a Hostile Environment

content_html_sanitized:
Please pardon the ponderous headline, but let Wikipedia explain.

 

“Set and setting, when referring to a psychedelic drug experience or the use of other psychoactive substances, means one's mindset (shortened to "set") and the physical and social environment (the "setting") in which the user has the experience.[1] Set and setting are factors that can condition the effects of psychoactive substances.”

 

In this case, I think it is particularly relevant for medical cannabis users in the United Kingdom as reflected in this headline from The Guardian: “Cannabis users who are self-medicating run higher risk of paranoia, study finds. Those who take drug because of pain, anxiety or depression found to be more likely to develop paranoia than recreational smokers.”

 

At first, this seems counterintuitive. In the UK medical cannabis is available via special referral services, so wouldn’t patients feel more comfortable with it?

 

But the Guardian then quoted Robin Murray, a professor of psychiatric research at King’s College London, as saying, “Contrary to what it says on the internet, cannabis is not medicinal. We now have 40 private clinics up and down the UK dishing out cannabis supposedly as a treatment, and the things that they are giving it for are pain, anxiety and depression predominantly. And these are the things that we find are related to people getting into trouble and becoming more paranoid.”

 

So think about patients who have finally found something that alleviates their problems, but a politically powerful psychiatrist is saying that what helps pain patients around the world is really not medicine at all.

From 2007  Prophylactic State Violence: The Arrogance and Ignorance of Psychiatric Quackery. Bad Science, Worse Ethics, “Professor Robin Murray, from the Institute of Psychiatry, has recently attempted to simplify the statistics. In the most recent comprehensive review of the research he estimates that the elimination of cannabis use in the UK would reduce the incidence of schizophrenia by approximately 8 per cent.”

 

From yesterday,

Over Forty Percent of Patients In Medical Cannabis Pain Study Stay In Program For A Year, Says Report

From 2000,

80% of UK Doctors " would prescribe cannabis if they were allowed to. "

 

I have known a lot of chronic pain patients over the years, and before medical cannabis laws were implemented, they really did live in fear of being tortured - and that is the appropriate word - by a government whose Constitution actually prohibits “cruel and unusual punishments.”

 

See Lest We Forget: From Twenty Years Ago, July 12,2005:The Murder of Steve McWilliams. An Indictment, Not An Obituary. The Absurdity of Evil. Condolences from NORML.

And from 2025

The Wall Street Journal Carries Excellent Story About The Outrageous Medical Abuse of Veterans: But No Mention of Medical Cannabis 

 

On the other hand, if I were one of the UK’s millions of illegal recreational cannabis users, I would not worry about being arrested, given all the serious problems that the UK has.

See

Beyond Parody, Actual Headline in London Tabloid:“Top police chiefs say smell of cannabis is a 'sign of crime' that can make even them feel 'unsafe'... and frontline officers should 'do something about it'

 

As Sigmund Freud said, “Even paranoiacs have real enemies.”

But, who’s crazy now?
